newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on speculation.

text.p: The Philippine peso nudged down to 26.343 at the close on Wednesday from 26.34 as banks played up the dollar amidst high liquidity in the market, traders said.
"There was nothing much that happened. It was just speculation," a dealer from a big bank said.
Traders said banks tried to test how high the dollar would go, but Central Bank sold dollars at 26.35.
"The Central Bank was taken for $40 million at 26.35 and he (the bank) stayed firm," another dealer said.
That sent the peso to recover some lost ground after hitting a day-low of 26.35 in morning deals, traders said.
The day's average was at 26.347 from 26.335, with volume rising to $174 million from $134.5 million.
"Long peso/short dollar is still the strategy," a trader said, citing the interest premium enjoyed by the peso.
The peso could be stronger on Thursday after the Central Bank capped its weakness, traders said.
